acceptance: Unit tests under a tmp lock dir prove: (a) contended acquire with WAIT_SECONDS=0 exits non-zero naming the holder pid, command and live waiter count; (b) after `kill -9` of the holder a waiter acquires within 2 s; (c) a descendant with the owner env skips acquisition; (d) an unrelated process given a copied owner env does not skip; (e) owner env with a wrong start time is rejected; (f) nested acquire in the same process returns without blocking and the lock is released only after the outer release; (g) a waiter whose fd points at an unlinked inode never reports itself as holder.

`python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run -- sleep 5` holds the lock (a parallel WAIT_SECONDS=0 acquire is refused) and releases it on exit; `make test-unlock` clears only an inactive lock and leaves an active one intact.
`git grep -n 'local_validation'` shows no remaining lock-helper callers; `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py` has no private flock/msvcrt code.
Existing `tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py` and data_fetch locking tests pass without weakening assertions.
Import-time numbers for G1 are recorded in the PR body.
`make comment-policy-check`, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make duplicate-check-delta` and `make test-fast` pass.

description:
## Problem
The host lock that serializes heavy work lives in `scripts/local_validation.py` and is loaded by file path from `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/utilities/session_isolation.py` and `_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py`. Product code (`benchbox run`, UAT, container wrappers) cannot reuse it. It also has three defects: a process that already holds the lock deadlocks if it asks again (a second flock on a new fd returns EWOULDBLOCK); the inheritance check trusts a bare PID, so PID reuse can make a stranger look like the owner; and a lock file that is unlinked and recreated lets a second holder run concurrently (`~/.benchbox/test.lock.stale-20260831-1504` shows replacement has happened). A second flock helper exists in `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py`.

## Change
1. New module `benchbox/utils/host_lock.py` owning all host-lock logic: open/flock/msvcrt primitives, holder record, wait loop, clear-inactive, ownership check. Move `seek_lock_byte`, `read_holder`, `write_holder`, `_close_lock`, `wait_on_fd`, `wait_for_lock`, `clear_inactive_lock` out of `scripts/local_validation.py`; migrate every caller (conftest, session_isolation, `_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py`, Makefile `test-unlock`) and delete the old copies.
2. Point `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py` at the same primitives so the repo has one flock/msvcrt implementation.
3. Lock path: `<real home>/.benchbox/test.lock`, real home from `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir` on POSIX and `Path.home()` on Windows; `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` still overrides the directory.
4. After every successful flock, compare `fstat(fd).st_ino` with `stat(path).st_ino`; on mismatch close and retry. Expose a `held_inode_matches()` check for later watchdog use.
5. Ownership: holder record and `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` carry `<pid>:<process start time>`. A process skips acquisition only if the owner is itself or an ancestor, the start time matches, the holder record names that owner, and the lock is actually held. Same-process re-entry returns the existing handle with a reference count.
6. Waiters register `<lockdir>/test.lock.waiters/<pid>`; the blocked message shows the count of live waiters.
7. CLI: `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run -- <cmd>` (hold for the child's lifetime, export owner env), `clear` (replaces `scripts/local_validation.py clear-test-lock`).

## Decision gates
- D1 (resolved): keep every existing name: `test.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER`. Renaming is out of scope.
- D2 (resolved): default wait stays 3600 s; `WAIT_SECONDS=0` fails fast. No automatic skip on `CI` or `BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE` (agent shells export `CI=true`).
- G1 (stop condition): measure `python -X importtime -c 'import benchbox.utils.host_lock'`. If it pulls non-stdlib packages or adds >100 ms over bare interpreter start, keep the module importable by file path from the pytest plugin (as conftest does today) and record the numbers in the PR before continuing.
- G2 (stop condition): if psutil is not a hard runtime dependency, get process start time from stdlib (`sysctl kern.proc` via `ps -o lstart=` fallback) rather than adding a dependency; adding a dependency needs owner approval.

## Guardrails
- Linked worktree from `origin/develop`; never the primary clone; stage paths explicitly.
- `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`: no comments or docstrings in new code. Durations use `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`/`elapsed_seconds()`.
- Tests use `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` under `tmp_path`; never touch the real `~/.benchbox/test.lock`.
- No behavior change for `-n 0` vs `-n N` acquisition in this item; that belongs to `heavy-guard-test-harness-20261030`.
- Do not delete, move or recreate a lock file from code; `clear` truncates only an inactive lock.

## Non-goals
Admission checks, watchdog, new acquirers, docs beyond the test-lock section that names moved helpers.
